analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and adds documentation near line 334 saying SIGHUP now enters the graceful drain for hand-started providers (start --local, start --foreground). The prose also says SIGHUP is not a stop signal for the launchd job, or when it was inherited as ignored (for example under nohup), and that a self-update re-exec carries the choice into the new process. It cites ProviderStopSignals.swift. The supplied units are BASE text only (cli-reference lines 861-1717). That text has no changed lines and does not include the new head text.

Security relevance: this is a lifecycle/availability change in the provider process. It does not touch the coordinator WebSocket, attestation, key custody, or prefix-cache controls (T-041 and others). A drain on SIGHUP is a graceful stop that should clear in-flight state like SIGTERM, and the in-memory X25519 key (A-003) lives only for the process. No new network attack surface, authorization change, or data exposure is visible. The threat-model assets and trust boundaries, including TB-011 and T-053, are unaffected.

Unverified: ProviderStopSignals.swift is not supplied, so the actual implementation is not reviewed. Examples to check: the SIGHUP-ignored inheritance across re-exec, and whether the drain deadline (DARKBLOOM_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) still bounds shutdown. These are docs-consistency items for a later pass if the source file appears in another batch. No concrete regression is claimed here.
